purpose: Translation layer — human phrase → trade concept — NOT an answer database. This file exists to close the gap between how homeowners describe things and how the trade names them. Every entry is expert-authored per Rule B. AI may cluster/dedupe/spot patterns, but the final translation ALWAYS comes from a named staircase expert.

two_file_architecture_philip_2026_07_30.this_file: How people think and speak — TRANSLATION layer. Answers: 'what does a homeowner mean when they say this?' Broad + shallow. Every trade concept the industry uses, with expert-authored people_say lists. Never contains full answers.
two_file_architecture_philip_2026_07_30.trade_terminology_ts: What an expert knows — RESPONSE layer at src/lib/nex/reflex/trade-terminology.ts. Narrow + deep. Subset of concepts where full definition + trade_insight have been expert-authored. Delivers the actual Reflex Brain answer.
two_file_architecture_philip_2026_07_30.why_two_files: Search engine knows 'riser = vertical part of stair.' NEX should know 'a homeowner might call this the upright bit between the steps · in staircase terms that's the riser · the riser affects the visual character of the staircase because it controls how closed or open the stair feels.' That second sentence needs the response layer. The first bit needs the translation layer. Both matter. Neither alone is enough.

governance.rule_b_no_ai_authored: AI extracts hypotheses. Expert approves. No AI-authored trade content ever enters this file.
governance.rule_c_attributable_origin: Every entry carries authored_by + verified_at. Provenance is traceable to a named human.
governance.anti_scrape_rule: NEX does NOT scrape the internet to populate this map. Own customer conversations + expert authoring are the ONLY approved sources.
approved_data_sources_ranked: 1. Own customer conversations (highest value · always available · properly consented · full context)
2. Search queries (external · manual authoring aid only · never automated ingest)
3. Forums (external · manual authoring aid only · never automated ingest)
4. YouTube comments (external · manual authoring aid only · never automated ingest)
governance.the_moat: Google has definitions. NEX has TRANSLATIONS — expert-approved, growing with observation, private to NEX. Every phrase Philip approves is one Google cannot copy.

response_style_options.explain_naturally_introduce_trade_term: Give the plain answer first, name the trade term inside the flow. Never lead with 'the technical term is X.' Example: 'That's called the tread — the horizontal part of the step you walk on.'
response_style_options.explain_naturally_note_variants: Give the plain answer and mention the main variants without listing every option. Example: 'That's a string — the side board that holds the steps. There are two common types: closed strings and cut strings.'
response_style_options.explain_naturally_connect_to_what_custom: Reflect back the customer's phrasing in the reply so they feel heard, then introduce the trade term. Example: 'The wooden bit on the side of your stairs is called the string. If it's coming loose...'

authoring_queue_for_philip.instruction: For each symptom above, author the probable_causes_by_expert array. Each cause should carry: cause (short label) · explanation (one plain-English sentence a homeowner understands) · fix_direction (short trade guidance · one sentence · never step-by-step DIY instructions). Once populated, set awaiting_expert_causes: false and add authored_by + verified_at. When the Expert Brain is later formalised, these become the diagnostic knowledge the composer draws from when BRAIN: expert fires on a diagnosis_* signal.
priority_order_suggested: 1. squeaks_or_creaks — highest homeowner search volume · most common Expert routing target
2. movement_or_flex — safety-adjacent · Expert must be crisp because Emotion will often override to Safety
3. separation_or_gaps — very common on older staircases · easy to diagnose from photo
4. damage_or_decay — installer / repair conversations · fewer but higher-stakes
5. uneven_or_inconsistent — often a survey question · overlaps with regulations (Part K)
6. finish_failure — lower urgency · finish is a cosmetic / maintenance decision
authoring_queue_for_philip.what_ai_may_do: Cluster incoming customer phrases into these 6 symptom buckets · flag phrases that don't fit any bucket (that's a new symptom worth naming) · never invent a cause · never rank causes without expert approval.
authoring_queue_for_philip.what_ai_may_not_do: Author probable_causes_by_expert entries · fabricate what a symptom 'usually means' · guess a fix · say 'this is probably X' without an expert-authored cause backing the statement.

priority_ranked_2026_07_30.priority_rationale: Tier 1 words are what people encounter when buying or renovating — highest ROI for the moat. Tier 2 are more trade-internal (fine for the Core 100 milestone but lower urgency). Tier 3 are decorative details customers rarely mention by name — nice-to-have. Ship tier 1 concepts first.

instructions_for_expert_authoring: 1. Pick a concept from the queue above (or observe a miss in a real conversation).
2. List 5-10 real human phrasings a homeowner would use to describe it. Prefer shape/location/problem descriptions over 'what is X?' — homeowners rarely know the name.
3. List 1-3 common_confusions the expert has seen customers make (e.g. 'people confuse riser with tread'). Optional but strongly encouraged — expert catches nuance a definition can't.
4. Set nex_response_style from response_style_options above (or add a new one if genuinely needed).
6. If full definition + trade_insight exist in trade-terminology.ts, set reflex_entry_exists: true. If not, set reflex_entry_status: 'awaiting_expert_definition' and note what's needed.
7. Never let AI generate the people_say or common_confusions entries. Extract from real observed conversations OR draw from your own expert knowledge of how customers actually talk.
high_value_phrase_patterns_philip_2026_0: NOTE: Homeowners rarely know trade names. They describe shape · location · problem. The highest-value people_say entries are the ones that DON'T contain the trade term. If a candidate phrase already contains the trade term (e.g. 'what is a riser?'), it's already caught by the existing term/alias match — don't bloat people_say with it.

usage_notes.how_runtime_uses_this_file: V1: source of truth for expert-authored translations. V2 (future): Reflex Brain loads this at build time and merges people_say entries into trade-terminology.ts customer_phrases[]. V3 (future): Composer uses this map to translate customer phrasing to trade terms BEFORE routing to Wisdom Brain, so the Wisdom prompt sees the professional vocabulary while preserving the customer's actual wording for context.
usage_notes.why_two_files_coexist: trade-terminology.ts is the runtime-loaded typed structure with full expert entries (definition + trade_insight). human-language-map.json is the broader translation asset — every concept the trade uses, even ones without full Reflex entries yet. The map is broad + shallow; the terminology is narrow + deep. Both are expert-authored. Neither is AI-generated.
